result:
I saved the results to `answer.json`. The Python calculation and a separate SQL query gave the same numbers.

| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| a. Segment with the highest Q3 net sales | `enterprise`, 306,373,324 KRW (consumer is close behind at 304,006,895) |
| b. Customers with a paid Q3 order | 244 |
| c. Category with the highest Q3 net sales | `sw`, 272,994,304 KRW |
| d. Month with the highest net sales | `2025-07` (321,849,285 KRW) |
| e. Customer with the largest Q3 refunds | `u12@ex.com` (3,473,500 KRW) |
| f. Customers with 2 or more paid Q3 orders | 234 |
| g. Average net sales per order | 702,757 KRW (867,905,745 ÷ 1,235 orders) |
| h. September vs. August growth | −14.6% (294,514,552 → 251,541,908 KRW) |

Things I found in the data and how I handled them:
- **Segments:** the raw values have inconsistent spacing and capitals (e.g. `' consumer'`, `'Enterprise '`, `'SMB'`). After trimming and lowercasing they collapse into three segments: enterprise, consumer and smb.
- **Duplicate customer accounts:** there are 300 customer accounts but only 250 distinct emails. For b, e and f I grouped by email, so each person counts once.
- **Order status:** I counted only `paid` orders and excluded `cancelled` and `pending`. Every Q3 paid order has at least one line item.
- **Refunds:** every refund matches an existing order line, and no refund quantity is larger than the quantity ordered.
- **Data period:** after converting to Korean time (UTC+9), the data runs from 2025-05 to 2025-10. October is incomplete (it ends on the 28th, UTC), but it still doesn't affect question d.
